newsitem.title: USA: Meredith sees momentum entering fiscal '98.
newsitem.headline: Meredith sees momentum entering fiscal '98.

text.p: Meredith Corp said Tuesday it starts fiscal year 1998 with momentum from strong earnings and is well-positioned from strong operations.

"The strength of each of our operations positions us well, and we're beginning fiscal 1998 with strong earnings momentum," said president and chief executive officer William Kerr in a statement accompanying earnings. "All of our business segments reported increased operating profits for the year and the quarter, with record results in publishing and broadcasting for both periods."
Meredith Corp Tuesday reported fourth-quarter June 30 EPS of $0.36 versus $0.28.

The company said its fiscal 1997 revenues from continuing operations were held down by fiscal 1996 actions that included selling the company's book clubs, closing home garden and Weekend Woodworking magazines, reducing the rate base at Ladies' Home Journal magazine and cutting the number of issues published by Country America magazine to six from 10 annually.
It said without those actions, company revenues would have risen about four percent for the fiscal year.

Meredith Corp is a leading media and marketing company with business centered on magazine and book publishing, television broadcasting, residential real estate marketing and franchising, and brand licensing.
